rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
$$\lambda=\frac{h}{mv}=\frac{h}{p}=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2mKE}}$$
$$\lambda_{\text{electron}}=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2meV}}=\frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}}\ \text{Å}\quad (V\text{ in volts})$$
$$n\lambda=2\pi r\;\Rightarrow\;mvr=\frac{nh}{2\pi}$$

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ Matter waves are electromagnetic waves. ✅ They are probability (matter) waves carrying no charge; they are not E–B oscillations.  ·  ❌ Heavier bodies have longer wavelengths. ✅ λ = h/mv — larger mass means a *shorter* (unobservable) wavelength.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: de Broglie proposed matter waves in his 1924 PhD thesis and won the 1929 Nobel Prize in Physics.  ·  Davisson and Germer confirmed electron diffraction in 1927 (Nobel Prize 1937).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: **Problem:** de Broglie wavelength of an electron moving at 10⁶ m s⁻¹. **Solution:** λ = 6.626×10⁻³⁴/(9.11×10⁻³¹ × 10⁶) = 7.27 × 10⁻¹⁰ m = 0.727 nm.  ·  **Problem:** Wavelength of a 1.0 g bullet moving at 300 m s⁻¹. **Solution:** λ = 6.626×10⁻³⁴/(10⁻³ × 300) = 2.2 × 10⁻³³ m — many orders of magnitude smaller than any aperture, so no diffraction is observed.

rows.text: Covers only: elementary idea of quantum mechanical model: de broglie's… (within Atomic Structure).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ### 1. Meaning — dual nature of matter  ·  Light behaves both as a wave and as a stream of particles (photons). In 1924 Louis de Broglie proposed the converse for matter: every moving material particle has a wave associated with it. These waves are called **matter waves** or de Broglie waves, and the hypothesis is the bridge from Bohr's orbits to the quantum-mechanical model.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: λ for a 100 V electron ≈ 1.23 Å; a 1 g body at 1 m s⁻¹ has λ ≈ 6.6 × 10⁻³¹ m — undetectable.  ·  answer pattern for "Elementary idea of quantum mechanical model: de Broglie's…": define → method → result. Structure earns the marks on 6–10 mark questions.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ### 2. de Broglie's wave equation  ·  For a particle of mass m moving with speed v, wavelength $\lambda=\frac{h}{mv}=\frac{h}{p}$; using kinetic energy, $\lambda=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2mKE}}$; for an electron accelerated through a potential difference V volts, $\lambda=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2meV}}=\sqrt{\frac{150}{V}}\ \text{Å}\approx\frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}}\ \text{Å}$.…  ·  ### 3. Meaning of the numbers

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: $$\lambda=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2meV}}=\frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}}\ \text{Å};\qquad n\lambda=2\pi r$$  ·  $$\hat{H}\psi=E\psi,\qquad \frac{d^{2}\psi}{dx^{2}}+\frac{8\pi^{2}m}{h^{2}}(E-V)\psi=0$$  ·  $$\int|\psi|^{2}dV=1\ (\text{normalisation});\qquad |\psi|^{2}=\text{probability density}$$

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ de Broglie's hypothesis was accepted immediately on publication. ✅ It became convincing only after the Davisson–Germer electron-diffraction experiment (1927).  ·  ❌ de Broglie's waves replace Bohr's quantisation with nothing. ✅ They *justify* it through the standing-wave condition nλ = 2πr.  ·  ❌ An electron microscope uses electron particles and light waves together. ✅ It uses the electron's short de Broglie wavelength, not visible light.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ de Broglie waves travel at the speed of light. ✅ They travel with the particle (v ≪ c); the phase velocity even exceeds c, while the group velocity equals v.  ·  ❌ The derivation needs relativistic mass. ✅ For non-relativistic particles λ = h/mv directly; the photon derivation only motivates the form.  ·  ❌ Davisson–Germer proved light has particle nature. ✅ It proved *electrons* have wave nature — the converse of the photoelectric effect.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ ψ is a measurable wave like a light wave. ✅ ψ is a probability amplitude; only |ψ|² is physically meaningful.  ·  ❌ Quantum numbers are put in by hand. ✅ They emerge from solving the equation with boundary conditions.  ·  ❌ Solving the equation gives exact paths. ✅ It gives probability distributions; trajectories do not exist.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Problem:** Why does the equation give discrete energies? **Solution:** acceptable ψ must be continuous, single-valued and normalisable; these boundary conditions are satisfied only for special values of E — the same logic that quantises a vibrating guitar string.  ·  Keep mass in kg, speed in m s⁻¹ and h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s to avoid order-of-magnitude errors.  ·  Quote both the general form λ = h/mv and the electron form 12.27/√V Å.
